pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: Migration 0002 adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all three seeded rows are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
src/index.js item() adds '★ ' only for starred rows. Test 'AC-2' asserts exact list output with one starred item.
The starred view filters with WHERE starred = 1 ORDER BY id. Test 'AC-3' stars ids 3 and 1 and expects them in id order.
Test 'AC-4' checks both / and /?show=all return all items in id order, with ★ on the starred one.

Test 'AC-5' asserts both links' exact HTML, so it would fail if either were broken. The spec's 'verified by review: checked by hand' is not a real step, but the named test is the evidence. The late edit to this item is a separate finding.
Object.hasOwn guard returns 400. Test 'AC-6' covers Starred, none, an empty value and __proto__, and checks that no <li> is rendered.
traffic/routes.json contains /?show=starred. Test 'AC-7' checks it, and the checker and fake app now accept queries.

findings.what: Commit 2f8eecb 'Follow-up edits' changed AC-5 after the go (2026-10-12). It appended '— verified by review: checked by hand', which splices into the middle of the sentence and breaks it. The spec records no owner decision for this edit. 'Checked by hand' is also not a followable review step. It reads as an attempt to turn the item into a review-only item.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-5 edit. If the item really must change, record the owner's call and its date in Decisions. Keep AC-5 proven by its test.

findings.what: The PR body says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but commit 2f8eecb edited acceptance item AC-5 after the go.
findings.fix: State the AC-5 edit under 'Changed after the go' and have the owner confirm it, or revert the edit.

lenses.note: The spec exists and the change follows its decisions: order is unchanged, and the view is a GET query parameter.
All four state-table rows have tests. A late commit edited AC-5 without a recorded decision.

The tests assert behaviour and cover each AC and state. I did not run them here (CI runs them). The loosened-test claim holds: the fake app change in traffic.test.js is additive, and new bad-route cases were added.
The README mentions ?show=starred. It does not mention the 400 for other values, which is minor.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, and the SQL is built only from fixed view strings. No defects found.
Input is whitelisted, titles are HTML-escaped, and no user input reaches the SQL. No instructions are planted in the repo content.
The diff touches the HTML output in src/index.js. Markup is minimal (a nav link and a star prefix), with no styling changes.
The page is rendered HTML, but the PR has no screenshots or browser run. The tests check the HTML output for each state.
The title is under 72 characters. The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false (see finding).
